long_biography.plain_text:
American entrepreneur Junior Bridgeman learned restaurant management during a difficult Milwaukee winter, when snow kept customers away and payroll became a struggle. He sought advice from other franchisees and worked eighteen-hour days in the stores. He came to see understanding employees’ needs as central to getting them behind the business.

His attention to service also shaped how he trained managers. He gave them copies of Raving Fans, a book he had used while trying to attract more customers, and helped entry-level staff progress into management. At his later company headquarters, a chef prepared fresh meals for his senior team each day.
